title: Impacts of PM2.5 air pollution on high-skilled worker productivity in China
title_zh: 中国高技能工人生产力受PM2.5空气污染影响
abstract: The short-term impact of air pollution on labour productivity has mainly been studied in the context of physically demanding occupations. Here we examined the causal impact of air pollution on the academic publications of individual scholars in China. Using an instrumental variable design and combining air quality data with a bibliographic dataset of publications, we found that an increase of 1 μg m−3 in the annual concentration of PM2.5 (particles smaller than 2.5 μm in diameter) causes a decline of 0.23% (P < 0.01; 95% confidence interval, −0.0028 to −0.0017) in publications. The mean PM2.5 concentration was 45.91 over the study period. A 1% increase in PM2.5 concentration results in a reduction of approximately 1,053 publications nationwide. This effect was more pronounced during years of heavy pollution, especially among highly productive and younger scholars. Further analyses showed that higher pollution levels reduced academic working hours, increased hospital visits and hindered scholarly collaborations. Dong, Qiao and Zhou show how variations in the level of air pollution impact the productivity of scholarly researchers in China.
abstract_zh: 短期空气污染对劳动生产力的影响主要研究在体力密集型职业背景下。本研究通过结合空气质量数据与个人学者的出版物数据库，利用工具变量设计，考察了空气污染对中国学者学术出版物的因果影响。研究发现，年度PM2.5（直径小于2.5微米颗粒）浓度每增加1 μg m−3，会导致出版物数量下降0.23%（P<0.01；95%置信区间，−0.0028至−0.0017）。研究期间的平均PM2.5浓度为45.91。PM2.5浓度每增加1%，全国出版物数量将减少约1,053篇。该效应在重污染年份更为显著，尤其影响高产出和年轻学者。进一步分析表明，较高的污染水平缩短了学术工作时间，增加了就医次数，并阻碍了学术合作。Dong、Qiao和 Zhou展示了空气污染水平如何影响中国学者的生产力。
